title: Cross-Functional Reliability Guild Onboarding and Incident Handshake
content:
Overview:
This doc defines a lightweight, repeatable program for onboarding cross-functional reliability liaisons (the Reliability Guild) and a clear incident "handshake" process so feature teams, platform, and SREs can agree SLOs, ownership, and operational readiness. Goal: reduce ambiguity at handoff, shorten time-to-stable, and create a minimal, testable contract for live services.

Why this exists (short):
- Too many features reach production without a succinct operational contract (SLO + error budget + escalation path).
- Teams use different measurement windows and alerting expectations.
- Post-incident root causes often trace to unclear runbook ownership and missing canary/rollback criteria.

Principles (how we design the program):
- Minimal friction: onboarding is a 2-week lightweight sequence, not a large audit.
- Liaison-first: each product/feature team designates a Reliability Liaison as the single cross-team contact.
- Contractual SLOs: SLOs are negotiated, written, and stored with a clear measurement query and alert thresholds.
- Incident handshake: a one-page summary accompanies deployment; if criteria unmet, feature may be gated.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Reliability Liaison (from feature team): coordinates readiness work, owns the feature-side runbook, primary on-call handoff contact for the first 30 days post-launch.
- Platform Engineering Liaison: ensures infra-level metrics, autoscaling, and deployment hooks are configured.
- SRE Partner: validates SLO definitions, test harnesses, and rollback criteria; signs off on monitoring and alerting.
- Product/PM Stakeholder: approves the availability targets in context of business impact and chooses acceptable error budget policy.

Onboarding flow (2-week template):
Week 0 (pre-start checklist) - checklist to complete before liaison kickoff:
- Identify Liaison and share Slack handle + pager info.
- Provide link to feature design doc and expected traffic profile.
- Create initial measurement queries (latency, p99, error rate) in metrics repo.

Week 1 - discovery and measure setup:
- Day 1: 30–60m sync (Liaison + Platform + SRE) to map feature surface area and dependencies.
- Day 2–3: Platform sets up metric ingestion and a dedicated dashboard tile; SRE validates query windows (rolling/30d vs 7d).
- Day 4: Draft SLO proposal (objective, target, measurement window, burn rate escalation).
- Day 5: Quick smoke tests and an agreed canary gating plan.

Week 2 - validation and handshake:
- Day 8: Tabletop: runbook walkthrough, simulated alert fire drill (15–30m).
- Day 10: Finalize SLO text and save in SLO registry with owner metadata.
- Day 11–12: Sign-off: SRE Partner + Platform Liaison + PM.
- Day 13: Deploy to canary; monitoring watch window.

Incident handshake (one-pager that travels with deploy):
- Service name + version + Liaison contact (Slack/pager)
- SLO summary: metric, target, measurement window, burn threshold that triggers page.
- Recovery/rollback criteria: what symptom triggers immediate rollback vs mitigation.
- Top 3 failure modes and short mitigations.
- Runbook pointer (URL) and first-responder checklist (max 6 actionable steps).
- Postmortem owner and expected RCA window (usually 72 hours).

SLO template (text to copy):
- SLO name: user-facing-text-generation-availability
- Objective: 99.5% successful responses (status code 2xx + non-empty body) over a 30-day rolling window.
- Measurement: sum(successful_responses) / sum(total_requests) over 30d rolling; query id: metrics.slo.user_textgen.avail.30d
- Burn/alert thresholds: 99.2% => notify slack #reliability; 99.0% => page SRE on-call.
- Error budget policy: allow 0.3% monthly budget; at 50% spent, product PM notified; at 75% spent, temporary feature throttling discussed.

Triage and escalation ladder (practical):
1) Liaison attempts initial remediation for 15 minutes (watch logs, restart pod, toggle feature flag).
2) If unresolved, Liaison pages Platform Liaison (10 minutes).
3) If unresolved or symptoms escalate (customer impact), page SRE on-call immediately.
4) For P0 incidents: declare incident, assign incident commander (IC), begin timeline, and create incident channel.

Communication norms and templates:
- Slack channel naming: #incident-<service>-<yyMMdd>
- Incident channel pinned items: one-pager handshake, SLO link, runbook link, playbook checklist.
- Postmortem timeline: initial notes within 24 hours, RCA draft within 72 hours, final PSR in 10 business days or earlier.

Operational artifacts to produce (per feature):
- SLO registry entry (one line): service, owner, metric query id, target, window, escalation contacts.
- One-page incident handshake (attached to PR and deploy).
- Runbook with 6-step first-responder checklist and rollback steps.
- Canary plan and synthetic test list.

Measurement and validation approach:
- Automated monthly SLO report sent to owners summarizing burn, incidents, and trend.
- Quarterly reliability review (30–45m) with product + SRE to adjust SLOs if business needs shift.
- Randomized runbook drills: 1 experienced run per quarter per critical service; public scorecard.

Quick wins (low lift):
- Add Liaison field to feature PR template.
- Create a lightweight SLO registry UI page listing owners and link to runbooks.
- Standardize canary smoke tests across platform teams.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: teams delay nomination of a Liaison. Mitigation: require Liaison in PR checklist; CI gate warning.
- Risk: differing metric semantics (latency computed at different layers). Mitigation: canonical metric definitions in registry and a short conformance test.
- Risk: alert fatigue. Mitigation: two-stage alerting (slack then page) and burn-rate-aware thresholds.

Success criteria (6 months):
- 90% of new features have a Liaison and incident handshake at deploy.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for P1 incidents decreases by 30% for onboarded features.
- Runbook drill pass rate > 80% across services in the Reliability Guild.

Next steps and action items (owner tags):
- PLATFORM: add SLO registry endpoint and template (owner: Marco Li).
- SRE: create tabletop drill schedule and tooling for simulated alerts (owner: Emily Carter).
- PRODUCT: include Liaison field in PR and release checklist (owner: Priya Raman).
- FEATURE TEAM: nominate Liaison and complete Week 0 checklist before next deploy (owner: feature PM).

Appendix: example first-responder checklist (maximize clarity):
1) Confirm incident and severity (check SLO dashboard).
2) Post short summary in incident channel: what, when, impact.
3) Check canary/metrics for related signals (latency, error spikes, queue depth).
4) Try a targeted rollback or disable new feature flag.
5) If rollback not possible, apply circuit breaker or traffic-weight change.
6) Escalate to SRE if customer impact persists after 15 minutes.

Notes and open questions:
- How do private deployments (customer-managed) map onto this handshake? Proposal: require a ‘customer readiness’ badge and offline handshake with solutions engineering.
- Explore adding automated lint checks for SLO presence in PRs.

Document history and intent:
- Author: Aisha Patel, Platform Engineering.
- Created as a practical bridge between feature teams and SRE to reduce post-deploy churn and ambiguity.
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive but light-touch; feedback welcome — add comments or ping author.
